reasons: Claimed status is 'compliant' and the cited text supports it: Section 19.1 gives professional/workmanlike performance plus material conformance to documentation and specifications; 19.2 gives a 90-day Deliverable warranty (later of delivery or acceptance) and hosted Services conformance for the whole subscription term, which meets or exceeds the preferred 12-month software / 90-day services benchmark.

19.3 covers no-malicious-code and Applicable Law compliance; 19.4 supplies the required remedy ladder (re-perform, repair or replace, then terminate and refund Fees paid) and preserves non-exclusivity, so the rule's remedy element is satisfied.
19.5's disclaimer is limited to implied warranties and expressly does not limit any express warranty or stated remedy, so it does not swallow the express warranty — no walk-away 'AS IS' risk.
Consistent with a compliant finding, the redline is identical to the original paragraphs and no counterparty comment was proposed; nothing is over-flagged.
The failed deterministic check is a false negative: the period is written out as 'ninety days' rather than numerically, so the regex missed a compliant 90-day term.
